Directions: Read and study the sources about key compromises of the Constitutional Convention. Then use the sources to answer each question that follows.
Context: This excerpt includes resolutions from the Virginia Plan, drafted by James Madison and proposed by the Virginia delegates to the Constitutional Convention in `text(1787)`. In response, William Paterson proposed the New Jersey Plan.
Title: Source 1: [Adapted from] the Virginia Plan (1787)
Content: `bb(1)`. That it is the opinion of this committee that a national government ought to be established consisting of a supreme legislative, judiciary, and executive. . . .
`bb(3)`. That the members of the `text(first)` branch of the national legislature ought to be elected by the people of the several states for the term of `text(three years)`.
`bb(4)`. That the members of the `text(second)` branch of the national legislature ought to be chosen by the individual legislatures. . . .

`bb(7)`. That the right of suffrage in the `text(first)` branch of the national legislature should be according to some equitable ratio of representation—namely, in proportion to the whole number of white and other free citizens.
`bb(8)`. That the right of suffrage in the `text(second)` branch of the national legislature ought to be according to the rule established for the `text(first)`.
`bb(9)`. That a national Executive be instituted to consist of a `text(single)` person. This person is to be chosen by the national legislature with power to carry into execution the national laws.
